newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean shares notch slightly up on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean shares notch slightly up on Monday.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial index edged a notch higher on Monday but brokers cautioned that activity on the bourse would remain rather muted despite a lower than expected May inflation figure.
Annual inflation fell to 20.7 percent in the year to May from 22.4 percent in April.

"But everyone still thinks inflation will go up next month so there is not likely to be much activity on the stocks," one broker said, adding investors were likely to maintain a preference for the local money market.

He said he also expected some investor interest to be diverted towards the national dairy, Dairibord, following the government's announcmement last Thursday that it was sellig off 75 percent of its stake in the company to the public.
"So we might not be seeing much activity on the stock market for quiet a while," the broker said.

The industrial index inched up 2.59 points to close at 10,467.04 on Monday, with gains recorded in food and wine firm Cairns which went up 120 cents to 1,500 while agricultural investors Chemco added 100 cents to 4,600 and Zimbabwe Sugar Refineries put on 50 cents to 1,550.
Construction and plastic investors IHL were also up 50 cents to 2,400, while sugar growers Hippo at 1,600 and financial house Finhold at 550 both climbed up 20 cents.
Mining counters traded largely unchanged and the seven-share mining index also closed unchanged from Friday's position at 954.32.
